evidence_excerpts: The networks identified in the S-ART framework elaborates upon past conceptualizations of self and distinguishes between two functional aspects of self-specifying processes, (1) non-conscious sensory-affective-motor processing, referred to here as the experiential enactive self (EES); (2) an agentic, self-as-subject acting as awareness in the present moment, referred to as an experiential phenomenological self (EPS). The S-ART also distinguishes between self-specifying processes and self-related processes, which refer to the evaluative self-as-object, reflecting the autobiographical narrative reconstructed from the past or projected into the future.
text: S-ART distinguishes experiential enactive, experiential phenomenological, and narrative self-processing systems as targets of mindfulness-related modulation.
